paraphrase: Vājaśravasa, desiring (heaven), gave away all his possessions; he had a son named Naciketas. Seeing the gifts — cows that had drunk their water, eaten their grass, given their milk and were barren — the boy thought 'joyless are the worlds to which one goes by giving these', and asked his father 'to whom will you give me?' Asked a second and a third time, the father said: 'to Death I give you.'

paraphrase: Second boon: the fire that leads to heaven, where there is no fear, old age, hunger or thirst. Yama teaches the fire that is the beginning of the world, the bricks, their number and how they are laid; Naciketas repeats it, and Yama names it the Nāciketa fire and gives him a many-coloured chain. One who has piled the Nāciketa fire three times, joined with the three, doing the three acts, crosses over birth and death.

paraphrase: The one controller, the inner self of all beings, who makes his one form manifold — the wise who see him standing in themselves have eternal happiness, not others. paraphrase: There the sun does not shine, nor moon and stars; these lightnings do not shine, much less this fire. Everything shines after him who shines; by his light all this is illumined.

paraphrase: The goose seated in the bright, the bright one in the intermediate space, the priest at the altar, the guest in the house; in men, in the higher, in truth, in the sky; born of water, of cows, of truth, of the mountains — the great truth.
notes: Quotes RV 4.40.5.

paraphrase: What happens to the self after death: some embodied beings enter a womb for embodiment, others go into a stationary thing, according to their action and according to their learning.

paraphrase: The person who is awake in those who sleep, shaping desire after desire — that is the bright, that is brahman, that is called the immortal; in it all the worlds rest, and no one goes beyond it.

paraphrase: As the one fire entering the world takes the form of each thing it burns, so the one inner self of all beings takes the form of each and is also outside. As the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not stained by the outer faults of the eye, so the one inner self of all beings is not stained by the sorrow of the world, being outside it.

paraphrase: This eternal fig tree (aśvattha) has its roots above and its branches below; that is the bright, that is brahman, that is called the immortal; in it all worlds rest, and no one goes beyond it.

paraphrase: When the five senses of knowledge stand still together with the mind, and the intellect does not stir, that they call the highest state. They regard this as yoga — the firm holding of the senses. Then one becomes undistracted, for yoga is arising and passing away.

paraphrase: It cannot be reached by speech, by mind or by sight; how can it be apprehended except by saying 'it is'? It should be apprehended as 'it is' and as its true nature; for one who apprehends it as 'it is', its true nature becomes clear.

paraphrase: When all the desires that dwell in one's heart are released, then the mortal becomes immortal and attains brahman here. When all the knots of the heart are cut here, then the mortal becomes immortal — this is the whole teaching.

paraphrase: This whole world, whatever there is, moves trembling in the breath; it is a great terror, an upraised thunderbolt; those who know it become immortal. From fear of him fire burns, from fear the sun shines, from fear Indra, the wind and death, the fifth, run their course.

paraphrase: If one can know him here before the body falls away (one is freed); otherwise one becomes fit for embodiment in the created worlds. As in a mirror, so in the self; as in a dream, so in the world of the fathers; as in water, so in the world of the gandharvas; as light and shade, so in the world of brahman.

paraphrase: Knowing the separateness of the senses, which arise separately, and their rising and setting, the wise one does not grieve. Higher than the senses is the mind, higher than the mind its essence (sattva), higher than that the great self, higher than the great the unmanifest; higher than the unmanifest is the person, all-pervading and without mark; knowing him a creature is freed and goes to immortality.
